extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and performing slam poetry for competition: rules, performance expectations, and tips to make a poem clear, relatable, and score well with judges. Emphasizes originality, time limits, performance, and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / Written piece must be original
rubrics_metrics.description: The written piece must be original. The story being performed for competition needs to be your own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the poem is your own creation and not plagiarized or adapted from someone else's work. Originality is a basic eligibility/ethical requirement for slam entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to time limit (3 minutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each poet has 3 minutes to perform. Poets lose points for going over 10 or more seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While practicing, time yourself to make sure you do not exceed the 3-minute limit. Edit or adjust delivery so content and performance fit the time window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and relatability (keep it simple and relatable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your poem should be able to reach your audience the first time it’s heard. The poem should be clear and convey a message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read and perform your poem for family and friends before competing and ask what is clear and what is not. Choose themes many people can relate to (relationships, politics, religion, insecurity, family, social issues, etc.) so the audience connects quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance: rhythm and passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Your poem should have a rhythm that shows through your passionate performance. A slam poem moves the audience through different moods. How the poem is performed is at least as important as the content if not more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work on vocal rhythm, pacing, dynamics, and emotional delivery. If performance isn't your strong suit, use resources for reading aloud and managing stage fright; practice delivering to evoke mood shifts and audience response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice, feedback, and study of other performances
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice with Power Poetry. Submit your slam poem in a multimedia form to Power Poetry. Watch other slam poems for inspiration, to give/get feedback as you prepare for the stage!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recorded performances to study pacing, emphasis, and audience reaction. Solicit feedback, enter online slams, and learn from fellow poets and influential spoken-word artists to refine both text and delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging mechanism: subjective 0–10 scores from 5 random judges
rubrics_metrics.description: After performing, poets receive scores (0–10) from 5 randomly selected judges. Scores are awarded based on how much each judge likes a poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that scoring is subjective and depends on immediate audience/judge reaction; aim for immediate clarity, emotional impact, and strong delivery to appeal to non-expert judges. The randomness of judges is intended to broaden participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance constraints: no props, costumes, or music
rubrics_metrics.description: Slam poetry is a type of poetry competition where people read their poems without props, costumes, or music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design your piece and performance to rely solely on words, voice, and physical presence. Avoid incorporating external aids that are disallowed in standard slam settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form flexibility: no required formal poetic structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Slam Poetry doesn’t need to be a specific form of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use any poetic form or none at all; focus on content and performance rather than conforming to traditional forms unless it serves the poem's impact.
